Name: hole_backfill_static_counterfactual
Title: Which Counterfactual Is Item Credit? Hole, Backfill and Static-Procedure Replacement Give Different Per-Item Values for Retrieved Experience, and Only Backfill Predicts What Pruning Realizes
Short Hypothesis: For the same retrieved item on the same (game, seed), the leave-one-out value with an empty slot (hole: what CUE-R REMOVE, Shapley-RAG marginal contributions and DIG estimate) is neither the value that pruning realizes (backfill: the retriever serves its next-ranked bank item) nor the item-specific value beyond the type's procedure (replacement by a token-matched placebo carrying the static procedure sentence). For expert same-type items backfill credit is a fraction of hole credit and item-specific credit is smaller still; for planted wrong-procedure items the references coincide; and the realized loss from pruning the bank is predicted by summed backfill credit while summed hole credit over-predicts it.
Related Work: CUE-R (arxiv:2604.05467) measures per-evidence utility by REMOVE/REPLACE/DUPLICATE in single-shot RAG, replacing with distractors rather than the retriever's own next candidate, and reports no cost or variance. Shapley source attribution in RAG (arxiv:2507.04480) and DIG confidence gain (arxiv:2509.12765) are hole-based marginal contributions in single-shot QA. The local additive attribution taxonomy (arxiv:2607.14271) names the reference (what replaces the removed input) as a specification choice but does not evaluate references against a downstream decision; semantic-missingness baselines (arxiv:2508.14482) argue the reference must be a plausible state, which for a memory bank is the next-ranked item. On the agent side credit is set-level (UCOB arxiv:2606.29502; ExpSuite arxiv:2605.30712), agent-level (TreeMem arxiv:2605.04811) or write-action-level (HiMPO arxiv:2606.16285); utility-refining systems that prune (ReMe arxiv:2512.10696; SF-AMS arxiv:2607.22562) never state which counterfactual their score is meant to track. The program's nested-k logs give hole credit per slot for free; nothing gives the backfill counterfactual.
Abstract: Every memory system that prunes or admits items acts on a per-item score, but the score is validated (when at all) against removing the item and leaving a hole, whereas pruning realizes a different counterfactual: the retriever fills the slot with its next-ranked item. We measure, for the same retrieved item on the same ALFWorld (game, seed) with a Qwen3-32B reader over k=3 expert-bank sets, four references for the same slot: hole (k=2), backfill (rank-4 item from the same retrieval log), a token-matched cross-type placebo, and the placebo with the type's static procedure sentence prepended (Measurement C at item level). Credits are estimated per item class (natural expert, planted wrong-procedure, self-written, cross-type) at positions 1-3 with cells sized to +/-5 net, and additivity of each reference is tested by pruning 50% and 75% of the bank at random and comparing the realized loss with the loss each reference predicts. The contribution is a statement of what per-item credit is for: the reference that predicts the pruning outcome, its magnitude relative to hole credit per class, and its cost (one re-run per item-episode, the same as hole).
Experiments: Unit: (game, seed, position p in {1,2,3}) over 274 valid_seen+valid_unseen games, 2 seeds, k=3 sets taken from runs/sweep/k_sweep_final.jsonl (item ids in rank order). Arms per unit: FULL (natural k=3); H (item p removed, k=2); B (item p replaced at the same position by the rank-4 item of that log); P (item p replaced by a token-matched, within 10%, expert trajectory of a different task type); S (P with the type's static procedure sentence prepended, tokens matched by trimming P). Credits: c_X = success(FULL) - success(X), paired by (game, seed). Classes: natural expert (all three positions: FULL 548 + 4 arms x 1,644 = 7,124 episodes, about 6 h); planted classes are inserted at positions 1 and 3 in place of the natural item, and their H, B, P, S arms are identical to the natural class's arms at that position, so each planted class needs only its FULL-with-plant arm: wrong-procedure (procedure action swapped, e.g. heat->cool, clean->heat, receptacle swapped for pick-and-place), self-written (self-pool success nearest to the game), cross-type (nearest expert item of another type): 3 x 2 x 548 = 3,288 episodes, about 2.7 h. Pruning-realization cell: prune 50% and 75% of the expert bank uniformly at random, re-retrieve, run 274 games x 4 seeds each plus 2 extra seeds of the unpruned baseline: 2,740 episodes, about 2.3 h; compare the realized loss with f x sum_p c_H(p) and f x sum_p c_B(p). Consumer-swap arm (separate): natural class at position 1, arms FULL/H/B on the second local backbone (serving verified first): 1,644 episodes. Total about 14,800 episodes, about 12.5 h at 20 episodes/min on two replicas; both GPUs busy throughout; pre-registration before the first confirmatory cell; the natural-class position-1 H cell is run first as the positive control (must show c_H >= +10 net, expected from the k=1 vs k=0 contrast of +20).
Baselines and Ablations: Nested-k slot credit from the existing logs (k=1 vs k=3 vs k=7) as the free position-level baseline; k=1 leave-one-out excluded because it equals the k=0 contrast; hole vs backfill vs placebo vs placebo+static as a within-unit factorial; position (1-3) and set composition (natural vs planted at rank 1 vs rank 3) as manipulated factors; per-type breakdown (clean/heat/cool vs pick-two vs look-in-light); set-level static-procedure arm (Measurement C) as the reference for S; random-pruning realization at two fractions as the additivity test of each reference; backfill item similarity to the removed item (embedding cosine and same-object flag) as a covariate; second backbone as a separate consumer-swap arm; seeds as a factor.
Falsifiable Predictions:
- P1 (backfill is a fraction of hole): for natural expert items pooled over positions, mean c_B <= 0.4 x mean c_H. Falsified if c_B >= 0.8 x c_H with the 95% CI of the ratio excluding 0.4 (the rank-4 item is not a near-substitute). Arm: natural-class H and B cells (1,644 paired episodes each).
- P2 (class x reference interaction): the gap c_H - c_B is at least 5 net larger for natural expert items than for planted wrong-procedure items (where H, B and S should agree because any correct replacement fixes the harm). Falsified if the gap for wrong items is >= the gap for expert items minus 5, or reversed. Arm: the 2 x 2 (class x reference) cells at positions 1 and 3.
- P3 (which reference predicts the realized pruning loss): at f=0.75 the realized loss lies within +/-5 net of f x sum_p c_B(p) and at least 8 net below f x sum_p c_H(p). Falsified if the realized loss lies within +/-5 of the hole prediction or exceeds it. Arm: the 75%-pruned bank cell (274 x 4 seeds) against the unpruned baseline.
- P4 (item-specific credit beyond the procedure): for expert items in clean/heat/cool types, S recovers at least two thirds of hole credit (c_S <= 1/3 x c_H), i.e. most item credit is type-procedure credit; falsified if c_S >= 2/3 x c_H in those types (the trajectory carries object- or scene-specific value the static sentence lacks). Arm: S and H cells per type.
- P5 (consumer swap, separate arm): the c_B/c_H ratio for expert items at position 1 on the second backbone is within +/-0.2 of the Qwen3-32B ratio; falsified if it differs by >= 0.3. Arm: swap cell (FULL/H/B, 1,644 episodes).
Measurement and Noise Control: All contrasts paired by (game, seed); cluster bootstrap over games with seed as a factor for CIs; the known floor is +/-8 net at 548 paired episodes and +/-5 at about 1,400, so natural-class cells pool positions (1,644) and planted classes report +/-8 per position and +/-5.7 pooled; ratios reported with bootstrap CIs and only interpreted when the positive control (c_H at position 1 >= +10) holds; pruning cell uses 4 seeds (1,096 paired, +/-5.7) because P3 is a difference of two predictions; prompt hashes and token counts of every replacement logged so that H/B/P/S sets are reproducible; retrieval is frozen from the logs so no arm re-retrieves except the pruning cell, whose re-retrieval is the manipulated variable; per-type results reported but only pooled claims are confirmatory; vLLM prefix caching on for both replicas, workers tuned to the running queue (>= 8 per replica).

Risk Factors and Limitations: Hole credit at positions 2-3 may be near the noise floor (+7 net for items 2-3 combined), making ratios unstable there; the confirmatory ratio is therefore pooled and anchored on position 1. Backfill items can be near-duplicates of the removed item, which is the point but makes c_B small and its CI relatively wide. The pruning cell changes the retrieval distribution, which the archived memory_budget_confound idea warns about; it is used here only as the realization check of an estimand, not as a volume claim. Second-backbone serving is unverified. Results are ALFWorld-specific: procedure-bound value may make S recover more credit than in environments where trajectories carry instance-specific content.
Addresses gap: G5 (single-shot RAG intervention attribution has not been extended to multi-step agents with a persistent bank, and whether item credit transfers to the decision that uses it is untested); secondarily G1 (no per-item counterfactual exists inside an agentic memory system).
Not a restatement of: Brief bullet 'Marginal value of items 2-3 over item 1 = +7 net; of items 4-7 = +4' (nested-k slot credit): that bullet measures the value of a slot under hole removal; this idea claims the value of a specific item relative to its backfill is a different and smaller quantity, and that only the backfill quantity predicts a realized pruning loss. Digest card arxiv:2604.05467 (CUE-R REMOVE/REPLACE/DUPLICATE): that card replaces with distractors in single-shot RAG; this idea replaces with the retriever's own next candidate and with the type's static procedure in a multi-step agent and tests which reference predicts what pruning realizes, with cost and noise reported. Archived memory_item_value_reliability (6.12) claimed item value is context-dependent without an intervention arm; here every value is an intervention on the same (game, seed) and the dependence is on the counterfactual's reference, not on context.

Name: masked_harm_pairwise_removal
Title: Masked Harm, Masked Help: Single-Item Removal Mis-scores Conflicting and Redundant Co-retrieved Experience, and the Pairwise Correction Costs Three Re-runs, Not Seven
Short Hypothesis: In a multi-step agent, the leave-one-out credit of a retrieved item is masked by its co-retrieved neighbour in a sign-predictable way: a planted wrong-procedure item's harm shrinks when a correct item is co-retrieved (unless the compliance trap makes the agent adopt it regardless), and a correct item's help shrinks when a twin is co-retrieved (unless duplication has a dose effect). A pruner scoring by single removal therefore keeps the wrong item and deletes the redundant one; the pairwise-removal interaction term, obtained with one extra re-run per pair, recovers the decision at less than half the cost of exact Shapley on k=3.
Related Work: Shapley source attribution in RAG (arxiv:2507.04480) reports redundancy, complementarity and synergy among retrieved documents in single-shot QA but does not measure how much a single-removal score is masked or what decision error results. Cross-component interference in agent scaffolds (arxiv:2605.05716) finds 56% submodularity violations with exact Shapley at the component level, not for retrieved items. CUE-R (arxiv:2604.05467) shows non-additive multi-hop supports in single-shot RAG. The compliance trap (arxiv:2607.10608) shows agents adopt conflicting memory at the first exposed decision point and that repeated exposure amplifies the error, but leaves untested whether the harm depends on co-retrieved correct entries; controlled memory interference (arxiv:2608.07622) uses synthetic relationships without per-item counterfactuals. RoMeRL's memory-reward trap (arxiv:2608.02508) is the training-side symptom of the same masking. Interaction indices (shapiq arxiv:2410.01649; Shapley-Taylor arxiv:2403.13106) supply the estimand; the archived retrieved_set_disagreement_gate proposed a set-level gate without item-level ground truth.
Abstract: Per-item credit is computed one item at a time, but items are consumed as a set. We manufacture k=3 retrieved sets for ALFWorld (Qwen3-32B reader) whose pairwise structure is known: correct expert item E plus a planted wrong-procedure item W (conflict), E plus a token-matched paraphrase E' (redundancy), the navigation and procedure halves of E as two items (complementarity), and E plus its natural second neighbour (natural sets), each with a cross-type filler F in the third slot and, for conflict, a second composition with a natural correct item in the third slot and a third with W in first position. For each set we run FULL, minus-i, minus-j and minus-both on the same (game, seed), giving single credits, pair credit and the interaction term; exact Shapley (7 re-runs) is run on the conflict and redundancy cells to check that pairwise removal recovers its ranking. We report the masking ratio per class, the fraction of sets in which a single-removal pruner deletes the wrong item, the recovery by the two-player Shapley within the pair, and the re-run cost of each. The compliance trap and the duplication dose effect are the published mechanisms that would falsify masking, so the experiment adjudicates between them.
Experiments: Sets on 274 valid games; items: E = natural rank-1 expert item, W = E with its procedure action swapped (heat<->cool, clean->heat, receptacle swapped for pick-and-place), E' = paraphrase of E token-matched within 10%, E_nav / E_proc = E split at the first procedure action, N2 = natural rank-2 expert item, F = token-matched cross-type expert trajectory. Compositions: A = (E1, X2, F3); B = (X1, E2, F3) (position swap); C (conflict only) = (E1, W2, N2_3) (natural correct third slot). Arms per set: v(FULL), v(-i), v(-j), v(-ij) with holes (k reduced), paired by (game, seed). Shared arms v(E,F) and v(F) serve all classes, so per composition the distinct arms are about 11 (conflict: v(EWF), v(WF); redundancy: v(EE'F), v(E'F); complementarity: v(E_nav E_proc F), v(E_nav F), v(E_proc F); natural: v(E N2 F), v(N2 F); shared: v(EF), v(F)). Budget: composition A headline cells (conflict, redundancy, shared) at 4 seeds (6 arms x 1,096 = 6,576), remaining A arms and all of B at 2 seeds (about 16 arms x 548 = 8,768), composition C (4 arms x 548 = 2,192), exact Shapley completion on A conflict and redundancy (v(EW), v(EE'), v(E), v(W), v(E'); k=0 from logs) 5 x 548 = 2,740, consumer-swap arm (conflict A, 4 arms x 548 = 2,192 on the second backbone): about 22,500 episodes, about 19 h at 20 episodes/min on two replicas. Order: the W-alone positive control v(WF) - v(F) runs first; if |harm| < 15 net, W is strengthened (wrong object and wrong procedure) before any confirmatory cell, per pre-registration. Analyses: masking ratio = credit with neighbour / credit without neighbour; interaction I = v(FULL) - v(-i) - v(-j) + v(-ij); per-set decision: single-removal pruner deletes argmin single credit (seed-averaged), pairwise pruner deletes argmin of the two-player Shapley phi_i = 0.5[(v(FULL) - v(-i)) + (v(-j) - v(-ij))]; Spearman between pairwise phi and exact Shapley on the completed cells. Exploratory on natural sets: does first-procedure-action disagreement between E and N2 predict |I| >= 10 (AUROC reported, no headline claim).
Baselines and Ablations: Single removal (1 re-run per item) vs pairwise removal (3 re-runs per set) vs exact Shapley (7 re-runs per set) as the cost axis; additive prediction (sum of single credits) vs measured pair credit as the additivity test; position swap (A vs B) and third-slot identity (F vs N2) as set-composition manipulations; natural sets as the realism control for manufactured ones; W-alone and E-alone cells as the unmasked references; paraphrase redundancy vs natural-neighbour redundancy; second backbone as a separate consumer-swap arm; seeds as a factor.
Falsifiable Predictions:
- P1 (masked harm): |harm of W with E present| = |v(EWF) - v(EF)| is at most 0.5 x |v(WF) - v(F)|. Falsified if the ratio is >= 0.8 with its 95% CI excluding 0.5, which is what the compliance trap (adoption of the conflicting item at first exposure) predicts. Arm: composition A conflict and shared cells, 4 seeds (1,096 paired each).
- P2 (masked help): help of E with the twin present, v(EE'F) - v(E'F), is at most 0.25 x help of E alone, v(EF) - v(F). Falsified if the ratio is >= 0.75 (duplication dose effect as in CUE-R DUPLICATE and the compliance trap's repeated-exposure amplification). Arm: composition A redundancy and shared cells, 4 seeds.
- P3 (complementarity): the interaction of the navigation and procedure halves, v(E_nav E_proc F) - v(E_nav F) - v(E_proc F) + v(F), is at least +10 net. Falsified if it is <= +3 net, i.e. the procedure half alone carries the item's value (the procedure-bound result of the starting position points this way). Arm: composition A complementarity cells (548 paired).
- P4 (decision error): a single-removal pruner deletes W in at most 55% of conflict sets, while the two-player Shapley within the pair deletes W in at least 80%. Falsified if single removal deletes W in >= 75% of sets (its masking is too small to change the decision). Arm: composition A conflict cell, per-set credits averaged over 4 seeds, rate over 274 sets (+/-6 points).
- P5 (position dependence of masking): the P1 masking ratio in composition B (W first) exceeds that in composition A by at least 0.3 (earlier exposure makes W adopted before E is read). Falsified if the difference is <= 0.1 in either direction. Arm: composition A vs B conflict cells.
- P6 (pairwise recovers Shapley): Spearman between the two-player phi and exact Shapley across conflict and redundancy sets is >= 0.8. Falsified if <= 0.5 (the third item's interactions matter, so pairwise removal does not suffice). Arm: the Shapley-completed cells.
Measurement and Noise Control: All contrasts paired by (game, seed); +/-8 net per 548-episode cell and +/-5.7 per 1,096-cell; ratio predictions are differences of two cells (about +/-8 at 4 seeds), so P1/P2 thresholds are set 0.3 apart on bases the positive control must show to be >= 15 net (W-alone harm) and >= 20 net (E-alone help, expected from k=1 vs k=0 = +20); cluster bootstrap over games with seed as a factor; per-set decision rates use seed-averaged credits and are reported with the per-set noise (binary outcomes over 4 seeds) so that the rate under pure noise (50%) is the explicit null; prompt hashes, token counts and item ids logged; retrieval frozen from the logs; both GPUs busy, workers tuned to the vLLM running queue; pre-registration of thresholds after the positive-control cell and before confirmatory cells.

Name: item_credit_variance_decomposition
Title: Is There an Item to Credit? Between-Item Variance, Re-run Cost and the Winner's Curse of Per-Item Counterfactual Credit in an ALFWorld Experience Bank
Short Hypothesis: Within a class of same-type expert items the true between-item variance of leave-one-out credit is indistinguishable from zero (item ICC < 0.1), so per-item scores over an expert bank fit re-run noise; item-level signal exists only between classes (expert vs self-written vs planted-wrong) and within self-written items, whose between-item spread is at least twice that of expert items. Consequently a stable per-item rank needs on the order of 16 retrieval-controlled re-runs per item, selection on fewer shows winner's-curse shrinkage of at least half, and pruning by per-item credit beats random pruning only when planted-wrong items are present and only above about 8 re-runs per item.
Related Work: Data Shapley (arxiv:1904.02868) and Data Banzhaf (arxiv:2205.15466, verified) show that leave-one-out and Shapley data values are unstable under stochastic training and that the Banzhaf value is the noise-robust semivalue; SCARV (arxiv:2605.00944) studies stable sample ranking under redundancy; FreeShap (arxiv:2406.04606) and amortized Shapley (arxiv:2305.19998) cut the cost of instance attribution. None decomposes item value into a between-item component and a re-run noise component, and none concerns retrieved experience consumed by an agent. On the agent side, TreeMem (arxiv:2605.04811) Monte-Carlo-averages branches without stating how many are needed, Shapley-RAG (arxiv:2507.04480) does not report attribution stability across repeated calls, HiMPO (arxiv:2606.16285) and AttriMem (arxiv:2607.21106) do not report the sample cost of their local utilities, and every scorer family (MemQ arxiv:2605.08374, RoMeRL arxiv:2608.02508, SF-AMS arxiv:2607.22562) presumes that items within a bank differ in value. The archived counterfactual_memory_screening_under_selection_noise assumed a noise model; the archived memory_item_value_reliability had no intervention arm.
Abstract: Per-item utility scores are the target of every self-evolving memory system, yet no one has asked whether same-class items in a bank differ in counterfactual value by more than the noise of measuring it. We take 100 items from the ALFWorld bank (40 expert, 40 self-pool successes, 20 planted wrong-procedure derivatives, stratified by task type) and force each into k=3 retrieved sets on 16 games of its type with 2 seeds, running FULL and minus-item on each (game, seed) with a Qwen3-32B reader; a 50-item subset is repeated with the item at position 3, a backfill arm is run for expert items, and a 60-item subset is re-measured on a second backbone. A mixed model decomposes per-item credit into class mean, item random effect, game effect and residual, giving the item ICC per class with bootstrap CIs. Subsampling the games yields split-half rank reliability versus re-runs per item, the winner's-curse shrinkage of top-decile items on the held-out half, and the number of re-runs at which bottom-decile pruning finds genuinely worse items. A confidence-gain proxy (first-action log-probability shift, one forward pass) is placed on the same reliability-cost curve. The result is the prerequisite every scorer paper skips: whether there is an item-level quantity to learn, and what it costs to measure.
Experiments: Items: 40 expert (about 7 per type over 6 types), 40 self-pool successes (same types, success-filtered on-policy), 20 planted-wrong (procedure action swapped in 20 of the expert items); for each item, 16 games of its type from valid_seen+valid_unseen where the item's retrieval rank is <= 20 (plausible retrieval), 2 seeds. Set = item at position 1 plus the game's top-2 natural expert items (excluding the item); arms FULL and HOLE (item removed, k=2), paired: 100 x 16 x 2 x 2 = 6,400 episodes, about 5.3 h. Composition arm: 50 items (25 expert, 15 self, 10 wrong) with the item at position 3: 3,200 episodes, about 2.7 h. Backfill arm for the 40 expert items at position 1 (rank-4 replacement): 1,280 episodes. Consumer-swap arm: 40 expert + 20 wrong at 8 games x 2 seeds x 2 arms on the second backbone: 1,920 episodes. Proxy: log-probability of the first procedure action with vs without the item from the same prompts, no rollout. Total about 12,800 episodes, about 11 h at 20 episodes/min on two replicas. Analyses: mixed model credit_{i,g,s} = mu_class + a_i + b_g + e with item ICC = var(a)/(var(a)+var(e)) per class, CIs by parametric bootstrap over items and games; split-half Spearman across items between disjoint halves of games at n in {2,4,8,16} games per half; winner's curse: top decile by half A, credit on half B, shrinkage = 1 - credit_B/credit_A; pruning: bottom 20% by half-A credit at n re-runs, mean half-B credit vs the pool mean; reliability-cost curve for HOLE, proxy and (from existing logs) nested-k slot credit. Order: the planted-wrong vs expert class contrast is run first as the positive control (must separate by >= 15 net at 40/20 items x 32 paired), before any ICC or reliability claim.
Baselines and Ablations: Class-mean model (no item effect) vs item random-effect model as the likelihood-ratio test of P1; expert vs self-written vs planted-wrong classes; position 1 vs position 3 composition; hole vs backfill for expert items; confidence-gain proxy and nested-k slot credit as cheaper estimators on the reliability-cost curve; Banzhaf-style robustness check on the position-1/position-3 pair as two coalitions; seeds as a factor; second backbone as a separate consumer-swap arm; random pruning as the decision baseline.
Falsifiable Predictions:
- P1 (no within-class item signal for expert items): item ICC for same-type expert items < 0.1 with 95% CI upper bound < 0.2. Falsified if ICC >= 0.3 with CI lower bound > 0.1 (expert items differ in value by more than re-run noise). Arm: 40 expert items x 16 games x 2 seeds, FULL vs HOLE.
- P2 (self-written items carry item signal): the between-item SD of self-pool items is at least 2x that of expert items. Falsified if the ratio is <= 1.2 with CI excluding 2. Arm: 40 self-pool items, same design.

Name: item_value_consumer_decomposition
Title: Whose Value Is It? Decomposing Retrieved-Item Counterfactual Value into a Consumer-Invariant Procedure Part and a Consumer-Specific Residual
Short Hypothesis: The leave-one-out value of a retrieved experience item is the sum of a type-level procedural part, which a static procedure sentence carries and which transfers across readers, and an item-specific residual that is reliable within a reader but does not transfer: on identical retrieved sets, the cross-reader rank agreement of item residuals is below half their within-reader split-half reliability, the residual concentrates in item classes that invite verbatim copying (long self-written trajectories), and value-guided item selection estimated under one reader is worthless under another.
Related Work: Per-item value is measured by intervention only under one generator: CUE-R REMOVE/REPLACE (2604.05467), document Shapley (2507.04480), DIG confidence gain (2509.12765, which explicitly does not examine transfer across generators). Agent memory systems claim model-agnosticism at the system level: ExpGraph/ExpSuite (2605.30712) swaps frozen executors and ablates modules, ReMe (2512.10696) reports that a smaller model with memory beats a larger one without, and CHIME (2609.02074) evolves separate planning and execution banks with attribute-before-memorize; none asks whether the utility of an individual experience learned under executor A is its utility under executor B. In the home literature, training-data value is known to be model-dependent (Data Shapley 1904.02868; DataInf 2310.00902) and proxy-model transfer of data-curation decisions is unreliable (2512.24503; DataDecide 2504.11393 finds it works only for likelihood-type proxies); this idea imports that question to in-context retrieved items with an intervention ground truth and a decomposition. The program's own memory_item_value_reliability (6.12) asserted that item value is not an item property but had no intervention arm.
Abstract: Every self-evolving memory system scores its items, and several claim the scores are model-agnostic, yet no per-item score has been re-measured under a second consumer. We ask whether the counterfactual value of a retrieved ALFWorld experience item belongs to the item or to the reader that consumes it. Holding the retrieved sets fixed (the logged rank-ordered ids from the k-sweep), we measure leave-one-out (REMOVE) and token-matched REPLACE effects of the same items under Qwen3-32B (reader A), Qwen3-8B (reader B, same family, weaker) and, as separate arms, a self-distilled LoRA variant of Qwen3-32B (reader C, the policy-improvement drift of G16) and a cross-family 8B model (reader D). We decompose each item's value into the gain of the type's static procedure sentence (Measurement C) and the residual measured with that sentence present. We manufacture item classes with enough retrievals for +/-5-net cells: same-type expert, planted wrong-procedure, cross-type token-matched placebo, short self-written and long-detour self-written. We test transfer at matched noise by comparing the cross-reader Spearman of item residuals with the within-reader split-half reliability of the same estimates, and we test the operational consequence by cross-fitted value-guided top-3 selection estimated under one reader and deployed under another. The contribution is a statement of what a per-item score means when the reader changes: which component transfers, which does not, in which classes the non-transferable part lives, and at what re-run cost the residual can be estimated to a stable rank.
Experiments: Setting: ALFWorld, expert bank, bank-target partition as in the starting position; 274 valid games (seen+unseen) x 4 seeds = 1,096 paired episodes per cell (~+/-5.7 net); class cells use 5 seeds (1,370, +/-5). Retrieved sets are frozen to the logged ids so the consumer is the only manipulated variable (retrieval is by task-text similarity and does not depend on the reader). Serving: reader A on GPU0, reader B on GPU1, both running concurrently, workers tuned so each replica's running queue stays >= 8. E0 (cheapest first, positive control): reader B nested-k sweep k in {0,1,3,7} on the logged sets (4 x 1,096); proceed only if B's k=3 net >= +10, otherwise report B as a non-consumer and switch reader B to Qwen3-14B. E1 ground truth per reader: k=3, REMOVE position 1/2/3, REPLACE position 1 with a token-matched cross-type item, k=1 (second set composition); pairwise removal of all three pairs on 1 seed (822) for the additivity test. E2 decomposition per reader: static-only, static + k=3, static + REMOVE 1/2/3; residual value of an item = REMOVE effect with static present; procedural component = static-only minus k=0 for the item's type. E3 manufactured classes at position 1 of the natural k=3 set, with/without: C2 planted wrong-procedure (expert same-type trajectory with the procedure receptacle swapped, e.g. clean with microwave), C3 cross-type placebo, C4 self-written same-type short (<= median length), C5 self-written same-type long-detour (>= 2x median navigation steps), 4 classes x 2 x 1,370. E4 cross-fitted deployment: item values (residual + procedural) averaged over an item's retrievals in fold 1 games are used to pick the top 3 of the top-10 similarity candidates in fold 2 games; cells: A-values under B, B-values under B, A-values under A, B-values under A, similarity top-3, random-3 from the candidates; ~1,100 per cell. E5 (secondary): readers C and D repeat E1+E2 only. Per-item analysis restricted to items with >= 8 REMOVE contrasts (expected 150-250 items). Budget: ~25,500 episodes per reader for E0-E4; at ~10 episodes/min for the single 32B replica and ~25/min for 8B this is ~2 days wall with both GPUs busy; readers C and D add ~12,000 each. Pre-registration of thresholds before E1.
Baselines and Ablations: k=0 and static-procedure arms per reader; token-matched REPLACE vs REMOVE (content vs length); k=1 vs k=3 REMOVE (set composition) and pairwise vs single removal (additivity); item-order shuffle control on 1 seed; same-family (Qwen3-8B) vs cross-family (Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct) reader to separate family distance from capability; self-distilled reader C to separate a policy shift from a backbone swap; in-reader cross-fitted selection as the upper bound and random-3 as the floor for E4; subsampling curves (rank correlation between estimates from n and from all contrasts) to report the re-runs needed for a stable per-item rank, compared with the LOO baseline cost of one re-run per item per episode.
Falsifiable Predictions: P1 (class-level transfer, positive control): under both A and B, C2 planted wrong-procedure < C3 placebo < C1 same-type expert, with C1 minus C2 >= 10 net in each reader. Falsified if under reader B all classes lie within +/-5 of each other or the ordering inverts; produced by the E3 class cells under reader B (a weaker reader can ignore item content, so this is not entailed). P2 (residual non-transfer): the disattenuated cross-reader Spearman of item residuals, rho_AB / sqrt(rho_AA rho_BB), is < 0.5 while the within-reader split-half rho_AA (seeds 1-2 vs 3-4) is >= 0.5. Falsified if the disattenuated rho_AB is >= 0.8 (residuals transfer) or if rho_AA < 0.3 (residuals are noise, so there is no item-specific value to transfer); produced by the E2 static+REMOVE cells under A and B on the same items. P3 (where the residual lives): C5 long-detour minus C4 short self-written is <= -8 net under B and >= -3 under A. Falsified if the C5-C4 difference is within +/-5 under both readers, or if it is more negative under A than under B; produced by the E3 C4/C5 cells. P4 (deployment): A-values deployed under B are within +/-5 of similarity top-3 while B-values deployed under B gain >= +5 over similarity top-3. Falsified if A-values under B gain as much as B-values under B (values transfer operationally), or if B-values under B gain nothing (the estimates are too noisy to use in-reader, a winner's-curse outcome); produced by the E4 cross-fitted cells. P5 (policy shift vs backbone swap, secondary): disattenuated rho_AC (self-distilled 32B) exceeds rho_AB by >= 0.2. Falsified if rho_AC <= rho_AB + 0.1; produced by the reader C cells. P1 is the positive control required before any null in P2-P4 is reported.
Measurement and Noise Control: Every value is a paired contrast on the same (game, seed, retrieved set): net = 100 x (success with minus success without), CIs by game-level bootstrap (2,000 resamples) with seed as a blocking factor, cells sized from the measured floor (+/-8 at 548 paired episodes, so +/-5.7 at 1,096 and +/-5 at 1,370). Item-level quantities are reported as distributions, never as individual effects; transfer is tested as a comparison of two correlations computed from the same number of contrasts per item, with split-half reliability estimated on the same items so that cross-reader disagreement is separated from estimator noise; Spearman SE ~ 1/sqrt(n_items) ~ 0.06 at 250 items, so a 0.2 difference is detectable. Additivity is tested by pairwise vs single removal; static-procedure credit is subtracted before any item claim. Estimator cost is an estimand: subsampling curves give the number of re-runs per item for a rank correlation of 0.8 with the full estimate, and LLM-call cost is reported per reader. Seeds and vLLM versions pinned; every arm logged as resumable JSONL under nohup with pid files; throughput reported per replica.

Name: stale_item_score_lag_after_rule_change
Title: How Long Does a Stale Item Stay Valuable? Score Lag and Co-Retrieval Contamination After a Manufactured Rule Change
Short Hypothesis: After a rule change that invalidates one procedure class in ALFWorld, the leave-one-out value of items encoding the old procedure flips from strongly positive to negative, but outcome-reinforced per-item scores flip only after a lag set by co-retrieval: stale items retrieved together with fresh post-drift items keep collecting credit for successes the fresh items produce, so the lag is at least three times longer in mixed sets than in stale-only sets, a large fraction of stale items survives score-based pruning after 1,000 post-drift games, and one-at-a-time confidence-gain scores barely move.
Related Work: Utility scores with forgetting or reinforcement are validated by aggregate accuracy only: SF-AMS dynamic utility from usage, redundancy and temporal cues (2607.22562), Oblivion's contribution-based reinforcement with decay (2604.00131), MemQ's TD(lambda) over a provenance DAG (2605.08374), budgeted forgetting by recency/frequency/alignment (2604.02280), usage-frequency plus externally validated freshness (s2:eddd4453). RoMeRL (2608.02508) names the memory-reward trap (jointly assigned trajectory rewards contaminate co-retrieved memories) but argues it from a coordinate-transition model, not from counterfactual measurement. Benchmarks show agents reuse invalidated memories (Memora 2604.20006; MINTEval 2605.18565; spatial staleness 2608.04574) and that agents comply with conflicting memory at the first exposed decision point (2607.10608), without attributing to items or measuring how a scorer reacts. Insight governance in non-stationary settings (2606.17591) shows the same experience can degrade or improve performance depending on curation, at the aggregate level. PlanFence (2609.03340) validates stale plans as a systems protocol. Home literature: rotting bandits (RAW-UCB 2604.21432) model arms whose value decays with time or pulls; prioritized replay (1511.05952) and replay staleness in LLM RL (2604.08706) treat priority lag. Archived utility_pruning_is_frequency_pruning was judged entailed by the pruning rule; this idea predicts nothing about usage-only scores (their non-flip is entailed and is used as a pipeline check) and instead measures the lag of outcome-reinforced scores, which is not entailed.
Abstract: Learned per-item utilities are asserted to stay valid as environments change, yet no study has watched a score respond to a known invalidation. We manufacture a rule change in ALFWorld with a command shim: after the drift point, the clean procedure's old command form fails ('Nothing happens.') and a new form is valid and listed among admissible commands (severity ladder: verb rename, then an added precondition step if the harm is too small to detect). Items in the expert bank that encode the old form are stale by construction; the pre-drift value of this class is the largest in the bank (+39 to +55 net), so the flip is maximal. We measure ground truth as leave-one-out and REPLACE effects of stale items on clean-type target games pre- and post-drift under manufactured set compositions (stale-only, stale + fresh, fresh-only, stale + fresh + other-type), then run pre- and post-drift streams and compute, from the same logs, the per-item score trajectories of one scorer per family (usage-decay, outcome-reinforced contribution, TD(lambda) over provenance, trajectory-averaged confidence gain) and of a leave-one-out-anchored online scorer that pays one extra re-run per episode. We report each scorer's flip lag relative to the ground-truth flip, its dependence on set composition, the false-retain rate under closed-loop admission with score-weighted retrieval, and the harm accumulated during the lag. The contribution is a measured account of what a utility score means after the world changes: which scorers see the flip, how many retrievals it costs them, and why co-retrieval delays it.
Experiments: Drift implementation: a wrapper over the ALFWorld text env that rejects 'clean {obj} with {recep}' with 'Nothing happens.', accepts 'rinse {obj} in {recep}' by stepping the underlying clean action, and rewrites the admissible-command list and observations accordingly (D1); D2 additionally requires 'turn on {recep}' first, tracked as a shim flag. Targets: clean-type games, ~45 valid + ~300 held-out train games whose expert items are excluded from the bank (bank-target partition), 350 games x 4 seeds = 1,400 paired episodes per cell (+/-5 net). D0 (cheapest first, positive control): k=0 vs stale-only k=3 in the drifted env at D1 (2 x 1,400); escalate to D2 if stale harm < 10 net; report the ladder. D1 pre-drift ground truth of the same items: k=3, REMOVE x3, k=0 (~5,000 new episodes, the valid part exists). D2 post-drift ground truth by composition, each with k=3, REMOVE of the stale item, REMOVE of one fresh item: stale-only (3 stale), mixed (1 stale at position 1 + 2 fresh post-drift self-pool items with the new form), fresh-only, cross-type-mixed (1 stale + 1 fresh + 1 heat/cool item); 4 x 3 x 1,400 = 16,800; pairwise removal on 1 seed for mixed (1,050); a stale static-procedure sentence arm (Measurement C with the old form) vs a fresh sentence to net item credit against type credit (2 x 1,400). D3 scorer streams: pre-drift stream of 1,500 train games (similarity retrieval) to learn scores, post-drift similarity-only stream of 1,500 games in which clean-type games are randomly assigned stale-only or mixed sets; because retrieval does not depend on scores here, every scorer's trajectory is computed post hoc from the same logs (3,000 episodes). Lag = number of post-drift retrievals of a stale item until its score falls below the median fresh-item score; reported as the median over the 60 most-retrieved stale items, per scorer, per composition. D4 closed-loop: admission of post-drift successes on, score-weighted retrieval, 1,500 post-drift games for the outcome-reinforced, TD(lambda) and usage-decay scorers (4,500) and the LOO-anchored online scorer at 2x cost (3,000); a fixed probe of the 45 valid clean games x 2 seeds at checkpoints +100/+300/+600/+1,000 gives false-retain rate (stale items above the scorer's pruning threshold) and probe harm vs k=0. D5 confidence gain is computed offline from forward passes on pre- and post-drift executed trajectories. Total ~38,000-41,000 episodes, ~1.5 days on two 32B replicas at ~20 episodes/min, both GPUs busy; pre-registration after D0.
Baselines and Ablations: Usage-decay (SF-AMS-style) as the entailed negative control: it cannot flip while the item is retrieved, so its trajectory checks the pipeline rather than testing a claim; LOO-anchored online scorer as the reference estimator with stated 2x cost; stale vs fresh static-procedure sentences to separate item credit from type credit; REPLACE (token-matched fresh item) vs REMOVE; set composition as the manipulated variable (four compositions); pairwise vs single removal; position of the stale item (1 vs 3) on 1 seed; drift severity D1 vs D2; a no-drift control stream of equal length to bound score drift due to sampling alone; the pre-drift bank's TD(lambda) provenance depth ablated (episode-level only vs with derived items).
Falsifiable Predictions: P1 (positive control, not entailed): post-drift, stale-only sets net <= -10 vs k=0 on clean targets while the same items net >= +30 pre-drift. Falsified if the post-drift stale-only cell is within +/-5 of k=0 at both D1 and D2 (the reader recovers from the admissible-command list); produced by the D0 cells. P2 (contamination): under the outcome-reinforced scorer, the median flip lag of stale items in mixed sets is >= 3x the lag in stale-only sets. Falsified if the lag ratio's 95% CI lies below 1.5, which occurs if stale items make mixed sets fail as often as stale-only sets (the compliance trap of 2607.10608 predicts exactly this, so the outcome is open); produced by the D3 stream with the random stale-only/mixed assignment. P3 (survival under pruning): at +1,000 games in the closed loop, the false-retain rate of stale items is >= 30% for the outcome-reinforced and TD(lambda) scorers and <= 5% for the LOO-anchored scorer. Falsified if the outcome-reinforced false-retain rate is <= 10%; produced by the D4 probe checkpoints. P4 (confidence gain is blind to the world): trajectory-averaged confidence gain of stale items on post-drift executed trajectories stays >= 50% of its pre-drift level while their LOO value flips. Falsified if the post-drift confidence gain drops by >= 50%, which happens if the reader stops following the item after 'Nothing happens.'; produced by D5 on the D2 episodes (the trajectories differ pre and post drift, so this is not an identity). P5 (lag is additive-inconsistent): single removal of the stale item in mixed sets and pairwise removal (stale + one fresh) disagree by >= 8 net. Falsified if they agree within +/-5; produced by the D2 pairwise cell. P1 must hold before any P2-P5 null is reported.
Measurement and Noise Control: All values are paired contrasts on the same (game, seed, set) with game-level bootstrap CIs and seed blocking; class cells of 1,400 paired episodes (+/-5 net). The lag is a per-item survival time; its median and CI come from a bootstrap over stale items (n = 60 most-retrieved) and the lag ratio's CI from paired resampling across compositions. False-retain rates are reported with Wilson intervals on the stale-item set per checkpoint. Scorer trajectories from the similarity-only stream share the same episodes, so scorer comparisons are paired. A no-drift control stream bounds the score movement attributable to sampling noise, and the LOO-anchored online scorer states the minimum lag achievable at 2x episode cost, so each scorer's lag is reported as multiples of that reference. Title: The Same Item, Three Moments: Stage-Conditional Counterfactual Value of Retrieved Experience in Multi-Step Agents
Short Hypothesis: A retrieved item's counterfactual value depends on when in the episode it is consumed: injected at the step where the procedure is due, a procedure-bound item delivers most of its entry-stage value; injected at a recovery point after the reader is stuck, an item whose trajectory is location-mismatched with the current game turns harmful while a location-matched one still helps; stage and stage-by-item interaction account for more of the variance of per-(item, game) value than item identity, so stage-free scores learned at entry mis-rank items for recovery-stage retrieval.
Related Work: Retrieval timing is a design choice in agent memory systems: SLEA-RL retrieves at each decision step conditioned on observation clusters and assigns step-level credit to actions, not items (2603.18079); MERIT argues memory usefulness changes across interaction stages and learns episode- and turn-level retrieval policies with PRM proxy rewards (2606.00547); U-EHR combines step-level credit with UCB-guided retrieval (KDD 2026). Abstract: Per-item utility scores are stage-free numbers, yet the value an item adds plausibly depends on what the agent has already done. ALFWorld is deterministic given the game file, so a no-memory prefix can be replayed without LLM calls and continued with or without an injected item; the paired contrast at each stage is a stage-conditional leave-one-out. Name: guilt_by_coretrieval
Title: Guilt by Co-retrieval: Measuring Reward Contamination of Learned Memory Utilities Against Leave-One-Out Ground Truth
Short Hypothesis: When an outcome reward is shared by all co-retrieved memory items, the learned utility of an innocent item is pulled toward the counterfactual value of whatever it is co-retrieved with (RoMeRL's memory-reward trap), and this contamination is a dose-response quantity: it grows with the fraction of an item's retrievals that co-occur with a planted wrong-procedure item, it is not removed by provenance-DAG credit (MemQ) or by reduced-order utility coordinates (RoMeRL) because both still pool siblings retrieved for the same task, and it is removed at a bounded cost by correcting a random 20% of stream episodes with one leave-one-out re-run per retrieved item. Contribution in one sentence: the first measurement of learned per-item memory utilities against intervention ground truth under manipulated co-retrieval, giving the contamination slope, the failure of two published remedies, and a costed fix.
Related Work: RoMeRL (arXiv:2608.02508) names the memory-reward trap and argues that fixed-dimensional per-task utility states limit contamination, but validates only downstream success, never an item's leave-one-out (LOO) effect. MemQ (arXiv:2605.08374) propagates TD(lambda) credit over a provenance DAG; siblings at one DAG level still share the outcome. REMEMBERER (arXiv:2306.07929) and MemRL (arXiv:2601.03192) update every retrieved experience toward the episode return. Memory-R2 (arXiv:2605.21768) and CHIME (arXiv:2609.02074) describe fair or credit-aware assignment for training or write-time policies but report no counterfactual check on stored items. UCOB (arXiv:2606.29502) and ExpSuite (arXiv:2605.30712) compare with-set versus without-set, which cannot split credit inside the set. On the ground-truth side, CUE-R (arXiv:2604.05467) and document Shapley (arXiv:2507.04480) measure per-item intervention effects for single-shot RAG only; Data Shapley (arXiv:1904.02868) is the home-literature ancestor of LOO valuation and reports that noisy per-datum values need many retraining samples. None of these manipulates co-retrieval as a dose or scores a learned utility by its rank correlation with LOO.
Abstract: Self-evolving memory systems now attach a learned utility to every stored item, but the utility is learned from a reward that the whole retrieved set shares, so an item's score reflects its neighbours. We measure this contamination directly on the ALFWorld expert bank with a Qwen3-32B reader. During one pass of the 3,553-game train stream we control, for a class of 40 bystander expert items with positive value in the nested-k logs, the fraction (dose 0, 0.25, 0.5) of their retrievals in which a planted wrong-procedure item of the same task type replaces the lowest-ranked co-retrieved item. Four scorers are learned on the same logs: per-item outcome Q (REMEMBERER-style), TD(lambda) over a provenance DAG (MemQ-style), reduced-order per-task utility coordinates (RoMeRL-style, reconstructed from the abstract), and a subsampled-LOO-corrected Q that receives an update only for items whose single removal flips the outcome on a random 20% of stream episodes. Ground truth is forced-retrieval REMOVE and token-matched REPLACE-static on the same (game, seed), measured under two set compositions (clean; containing a planted item). Each scorer is scored by its Spearman correlation with LOO, raw and disattenuated by the split-seed reliability of LOO, and by the false-prune rate at a bottom-quartile threshold. We test additivity with pairwise versus single removal on manufactured helpful+conflicting and helpful+redundant sets. Predictions: the per-item Q correlation with LOO falls by at least 0.15 from dose 0 to dose 0.5 while the bystanders' clean-composition LOO value does not move; neither MemQ nor RoMeRL coordinates beat per-item Q by more than 0.10 at dose 0.5; the 20%-LOO correction recovers the loss at 0.6 extra episodes per stream episode; single removals over-count the pair removal by 10 net points or more in at least 30% of helpful+conflicting sets. Every cell is paired, both GPUs run one replica each, and the whole study is about 26 GPU-pair hours.
Experiments:
- Ground-truth protocol (shared by all cells): forced-retrieval intervention on the same (game, seed). For a sampled item i of class C, take 24 same-type evaluation games x 2 seeds = 48 paired episodes with i forced into the k=3 set at rank 3 (the other two slots are the natural top-2 retrievals, or a manipulated composition). Arms per pair: WITH (i present), REMOVE (k=2 set), REPLACE-static (i replaced by the type's static procedure sentence padded to i's token count; Measurement C baseline, so REPLACE-static is item value net of the static prompt). Per-item effect = mean paired success difference; per-item SE about 0.10 at p=0.5; a 40-item class = 1,920 pairs gives a class CI of about +/-4.5 net. Cost per class per condition: 40 items x 48 pairs x 2 extra arms = 3,840 episodes = 3.2 h at 20 episodes/min on two replicas.

(a) Planted wrong-procedure class W (40 items, one per task type x layout, each swapping the target receptacle or omitting the clean/heat/cool step): REMOVE effect must be <= -10 net, else contamination cannot be manufactured and the study stops. (b) Per-item Q learned at dose 0 must separate W from bystander class B with Spearman >= 0.3 against LOO on the pooled 80 items, else the scorer implementation is rejected.

- Self-pool control: repeat E2 on 40 self-written items to test whether contamination slopes differ for self versus expert items.
- Token- and rate-matched placebo: the planted W item is token-matched to the item it displaces, and dose 0 passes receive an equally frequent replacement by a random same-type expert item, so the manipulation changes only wrongness, not set size or churn.

Name: admission_pruning_audit_random_holdout
Title: Admit Everything Once: Auditing Write-Time Utility Scores and Outcome-Based Pruning Against Realized Counterfactual Item Value
Short Hypothesis: Write-time admission scores (A-MAC-style factor admission, RPE-critic surprise/utility, DIG-style confidence gain) do not predict the realized counterfactual value of a memory item beyond rank correlation 0.2, so bypassed items are as valuable as admitted ones; and outcome-based pruning beats random pruning only for items that have accumulated at least 8 feedback events, a threshold fewer than one store item in five reaches in a 3,553-game stream, so most pruning decisions in a self-evolving store are made at random-equivalent precision. Contribution in one sentence: a randomized-holdout audit that puts admission and pruning error rates, and the feedback count a pruning decision needs, on an intervention scale.
Related Work: A-MAC (arXiv:2603.04549) admits by five interpretable factors and reports precision-recall against annotated relevance, not realized utility; the RPE-critic router (arXiv:2603.14597) gates writes by surprise and predicted utility and reports cost, not the fate of bypassed items; SF-AMS (arXiv:2607.22562) and Oblivion (arXiv:2604.00131) prune or decay by usage-derived utility and validate by aggregate accuracy only; ReMe (arXiv:2512.10696) utility-refines but does not report pruning errors; DIG (arXiv:2509.12765) scores documents by confidence gain one at a time in single-shot RAG. Memory Reward Inflation (arXiv:2608.00017) shows self-graded rewards inflate wrong episodes in text-to-SQL and proposes answer-free de-inflation; our rewards are environment-verified, so any entrenchment we find is not grading inflation. Utility-driven replay (s2:05c14833) evicts by reward magnitude and TD error on classic control. In data valuation, Data Shapley (arXiv:1904.02868) and DVGS (arXiv:2405.08217) rank data for removal but validate by retrain curves, the analogue of our forced-retrieval LOO; no memory system has run that curve for its admission or pruning rule. The archived idea utility_pruning_is_frequency_pruning was rejected as entailed by the pruning rule; this proposal audits outcomes, not the rule.
Abstract: Every self-evolving memory decides twice about an item: whether to admit it and whether to keep it. Both decisions are made from scores whose relation to the item's realized effect has never been measured, because a bypassed item is never seen again. We run a randomized-holdout audit on ALFWorld with a Qwen3-32B reader. All 1,892 self-pool successes plus 40 planted wrong-procedure items enter a shadow store regardless of any rule; three write-time scorers (A-MAC-style factors, RPE-critic surprise/utility, DIG-style confidence gain on one held-out same-type game) score every candidate. A stratified sample of 160 candidates spanning each scorer's quartiles is then evaluated by forced-retrieval ADD (item forced into the k=3 set versus token-matched static-procedure placebo) on 24 games x 2 seeds each, giving realized value on the same (game, seed). After one pass of the train stream with per-item outcome Q feeding retrieval, and a second pass with usage-decay (SF-AMS-style) utility feeding retrieval, we prune the bottom 20% by each score and a random 20%, and measure the pruned items' realized value stratified by feedback count (1-3, 4-7, >= 8). We report admission rank correlation with realized value, false-bypass cost (realized value of bypassed items), harmless-prune and harmful-item-capture rates versus random, the feedback count at which outcome pruning beats random, the fraction of store items reaching it, and the retrieval share of planted wrong items across stream thirds under the two utility rules. Predictions: no write-time scorer exceeds rank correlation 0.2 with realized value; admitted and bypassed items differ by less than 5 net; outcome-Q pruning beats random by >= 0.15 in harmful-item capture only at >= 8 feedback events; under usage-decay utility the wrong items' retrieval share rises across the stream. About 20 GPU-pair hours.
Experiments:
- Ground-truth protocol (shared by all cells): forced-retrieval intervention on the same (game, seed). For a sampled item i of class C, take 24 same-type evaluation games x 2 seeds = 48 paired episodes with i forced into the k=3 set at rank 3 (the other two slots are the natural top-2 retrievals, or a manipulated composition). Arms per pair: WITH (i present), ADD/REMOVE (item absent, k=2 set), REPLACE-static (i replaced by the type's static procedure sentence padded to i's token count; Measurement C baseline, so REPLACE-static is item value net of the static prompt). Per-item effect = mean paired success difference; per-item SE about 0.10 at p=0.5; a 40-item class = 1,920 pairs gives a class CI of about +/-4.5 net. Cost per class per condition: 40 items x 48 pairs x 2 extra arms = 3,840 episodes = 3.2 h at 20 episodes/min on two replicas.
- E0 Positive control, cheapest first (~3.5 h): 40 expert procedural items versus 40 planted wrong-procedure items under forced-retrieval ADD must separate by >= 15 net; otherwise the audit lacks power and stops.
- E1 Admission audit (~6.4 h of re-runs plus forward passes): shadow store = expert bank + 1,892 self-pool items + 40 planted W items. Three write-time scorers: (a) A-MAC-style factors (novelty = 1 - max cosine to store, task-type relevance, outcome confidence from the source episode's step count, redundancy with same-type items, specificity), combined by the published weighting where stated, else equal weights with a pre-registered threshold at the 60th percentile; (b) RPE-critic: surprise = reader NLL of the source trajectory's actions given the k=3 retrieved set at write time, utility = critic-predicted gain (a logistic model on surprise, novelty and type fitted on the first 500 stream games); (c) DIG-style confidence gain = change in reader log-probability of the successful action sequence of one held-out same-type train game with versus without the candidate in context (two forward passes). Sample 160 candidates stratified by each scorer's quartiles; measure ADD versus REPLACE-static on 24 games x 2 seeds each. Report Spearman(score, realized ADD) raw and disattenuated, and the realized ADD of admitted versus bypassed items per rule.
- E2 Stream passes (~6 h): pass A with per-item outcome Q (count-average) multiplying similarity in the retrieval rank; pass B with SF-AMS-style utility (usage, redundancy, recency) multiplying similarity. Log retrieved ids, positions, outcomes, and per-item feedback counts. Record the distribution of feedback events per store item and the retrieval share of the 40 planted W items per stream third.
- E3 Pruning audit (~5.8 h): for each of {random, outcome-Q bottom 20%, SF-AMS bottom 20%} and each feedback-count stratum {1-3, 4-7, >= 8}, sample 24 pruned items and measure realized LOO (REMOVE and REPLACE-static) on 16 games x 2 seeds. Metrics: harmless-prune rate (LOO <= 0), harmful-item capture (fraction of items with LOO <= -10 net that the rule prunes, using the E1 sample as the reference population), and the smallest stratum at which outcome-Q exceeds random by >= 0.15.
- E4 Composition check: the 40 planted W items and 40 highest-scoring admitted items are re-measured under a second composition (k=3 set with one self-written item swapped for an expert item) to test that admission-score rank agreement with realized value does not depend on the co-retrieved set (~3.2 h).
- Budget: E0 3.5 h + E1 6.4 h + E2 6 h + E3 5.8 h + E4 3.2 h = about 25 h on two A100s, one replica per GPU, E1 re-runs on one replica while E2 pass A runs on the other; nohup, pid files, resumable JSONL; pre-registration before E1.
Baselines and Ablations:
- Admission baselines: admit-all (shadow store), random admission at the same rate, similarity-to-existing-store threshold (novelty only), and the three write-time scorers.
- Pruning baselines: random pruning at matched count; outcome-Q; SF-AMS usage-decay; oracle pruning by realized LOO from E1 as the ceiling.
- Ablations: scorer components (novelty-only, redundancy-only, confidence-gain-only); DIG held-out game count 1 versus 3; feedback-count strata; outcome-Q with constant alpha versus count-average.
- Controls demanded by prior rounds: self-pool versus expert items reported separately; REPLACE-static placebo so admission value is net of the type procedure; token-matched planted items; both compositions in E4.
- Free baseline: nested-k logs give a position-level estimate for expert items to compare with the admission scorers on the same items.
Falsifiable Predictions:
- P1 (headline) No write-time scorer exceeds Spearman 0.2 (disattenuated 0.3) with realized ADD value over the 160-candidate sample, and admitted minus bypassed realized ADD is within +/-5 net for every rule. Falsified if: any scorer reaches Spearman >= 0.4 with a bootstrap CI excluding 0.2, or admitted minus bypassed >= 5 net with CI excluding 0. Arm: E1 forced-retrieval cells on admitted versus bypassed strata. Not entailed: E0 confirms that realized values differ across items, so a scorer could in principle track them; confidence gain in particular could.
- P2 Feedback threshold: outcome-Q pruning exceeds random pruning in harmful-item capture by >= 0.15 only in the >= 8 feedback-event stratum and by < 0.10 in the 1-3 stratum. Falsified if: the >= 0.15 advantage appears already at 1-3 events (large-effect items are identifiable from a handful of outcomes). Arm: E3 outcome-Q versus random within the 1-3 stratum.
- P3 Coverage: fewer than 20% of store items reach >= 8 feedback events in the 3,553-game stream under similarity x utility retrieval. Falsified if: >= 35% do. Arm: E2 pass-A retrieval log.
- P4 Usage is not value: SF-AMS-style pruning's harmful-item capture is within +/-0.10 of random in every stratum, while its harmless-prune rate exceeds random (it removes redundant items with LOO near zero). Falsified if: SF-AMS capture >= random + 0.20 in any stratum. Arm: E3 SF-AMS cells.
- P5 Entrenchment versus correction: the planted W items' retrieval share in the last stream third relative to the first is <= 0.7 under outcome-Q and >= 1.5 under SF-AMS utility. Falsified (Q part) if: the ratio under outcome-Q is >= 0.9, i.e. verified failures do not demote wrong items because the co-retrieved helpful items rescue enough episodes. Falsified (SF-AMS part) if: the ratio is <= 1.1 because redundancy and recency terms cancel the usage loop. Arm: E2 pass A and pass B retrieval logs. The SF-AMS part is the weaker prediction since the usage loop is positive feedback by construction; it is reported as secondary and the Q part is the tested claim.
- Positive control that must pass first: E0 expert-versus-W separation >= 15 net; if it fails the audit is reported as underpowered, not as a null.
Measurement and Noise Control: All value measurements are paired on (game, seed) with the retrieved set changed at one slot. Per-item SE about 0.10 at 48 pairs; quartile strata of 40 items = 1,920 pairs give +/-4.5 net. Rank correlations use 1,000 item-level bootstraps and are disattenuated by split-seed reliability of realized value; both are reported. The E2 stream pass is repeated for pass A with a second stream seed to obtain the test-retest Spearman of per-item Q, which bounds how much of any pruning imprecision is estimator noise versus rule error. Harmful-item capture uses the E1 sample's realized values as the reference set, with the -10 net cutoff pre-registered. Cost is reported per decision: forward passes per candidate for each admission scorer, and episodes per item to reach split-half reliability 0.5 of realized value. Throughput logged per cell; both GPUs busy by overlapping E1 re-runs with E2 passes.

Q2 [mechanism, --recent] 'reward contamination co-retrieved memory items utility reinforcement LLM agent': RoMeRL 2608.02508; Memory Reward Inflation 2608.00017 (verified via s2cli paper: self-graded reward inflation compounds under similarity retrieval, LUCID de-inflation on BIRD; closest to P5 but about grading, not admission or pruning error rates against counterfactual value); Memory-R2 2605.21768. Q4 home: 'data valuation predicted value versus realized value selection bias winner's curse shrinkage noisy estimates': DVGS 2405.08217, Data Shapley 1904.02868, Tweedie/linear calibration for prediction debiasing 2508.01341, HTE model-selection dilemma 2302.02923; nothing on admission rules for stored items, but the Tweedie correction is a candidate shrinkage for P2's low-count strata. Q5 home: 'prioritized experience replay priority staleness reinforced sampling wrong transitions bias': PER 1511.05952, HER 1707.01495, experience replay for LLM RL 2604.08706 (staleness-variance trade-off), Prompt Replay 2603.21177; the entrenchment loop is known in replay prioritization but has not been measured for stored-item utilities against counterfactual value. - Admission scorers are reconstructions (A-MAC factor weights, the RPE critic) from abstracts; results are stated for the reconstructions and any released code is run alongside.

- If fewer than 60 items reach >= 8 feedback events, the top stratum is underpowered; the fallback is to force retrieval of a 40-item subset until they reach 8 events (about 1.5 h) and report it as a manipulated stratum.

Addresses gap: G10 (error rates of admission, pruning and decay rules; predicted write-time utility versus realized utility; reinforcement of frequently used wrong items) directly, and G8 (feedback events needed for a stable per-item decision) through the feedback-count strata.
Not a restatement of: Nearest brief bullet: the self pool of 1,892 success-filtered items is described as useful for items whose value differs from expert items; this idea claims that write-time scores over that pool do not rank realized value and that bypassed items are worth as much as admitted ones, which the pool description does not measure. Nearest digest cards: RPE critic arXiv:2603.14597 and A-MAC arXiv:2603.04549 predict write-time utility and never see bypassed items again; this idea claims a bounded rank correlation with realized counterfactual value and a false-bypass cost, measured by admitting everything once. Name: utility_half_life_consumer_swap
Title: Harm Travels, Help Does Not: Re-measuring Learned Memory Utilities Against Leave-One-Out Value After Reader Swap, Store Growth and Layout Shift
Short Hypothesis: A learned per-item utility is a statement about one reader, one store and one query distribution: after the reader is swapped, the store grows with self-written items, or the layouts change from seen to unseen, the counterfactual value of helpful items collapses or changes sign while the value of wrong-procedure items persists, so the learned utility keeps its power to flag harm and loses its power to rank help, and re-validating it by intervention on a class sample costs fewer episodes than re-learning it from the stream. Contribution in one sentence: intervention-measured sign-transfer asymmetry of item value across three drift arms, with the lag and cost of the learned utility behind it.
Related Work: ExpSuite (arXiv:2605.30712) claims executor-agnostic experience reuse but does not isolate whether utilities learned under one executor hold under another; MemQ (arXiv:2605.08374) and MERIT (arXiv:2606.00547) learn values on a fixed stream and do not re-measure them; ReMe (arXiv:2512.10696) reports a memory-scaling effect without item-level transfer; the freshness-weighted memory (s2:eddd4453) and SF-AMS (arXiv:2607.22562) decay by time, not by measured value change; Memora (arXiv:2604.20006) and MINTEval (arXiv:2605.18565) show reuse of invalidated memories at the outcome level only; the continual-learning view (arXiv:2604.27003) relocates stability-plasticity to retrieval without item attribution; the compliance trap (arXiv:2607.10608) shows wrong memory harms stronger agents more, which motivates the harm-transfers half of the hypothesis. In the home literature, training-data attribution is evaluated by the linear datamodeling score (arXiv:2410.13850) and representation methods (AirRep arXiv:2505.18513) aim at model-aligned attributions, but transfer of attribution scores across consumer models is not reported for stored items. The archived idea memory_item_value_reliability (6.12) asserted that item value is not an item property; it had no intervention arm and effects under the noise floor. This proposal supplies the intervention under each condition, sizes classes to +/-4.5 net, and makes an asymmetric prediction that can fail.
Abstract: Learned memory utilities are trained once and trusted thereafter. We ask what they are still worth after three ordinary changes: the reader model is swapped, the store grows, and the query distribution shifts. On ALFWorld we learn per-item outcome Q over the 3,553-game train stream with Qwen3-32B and the expert bank, then measure forced-retrieval leave-one-out and token-matched replace-static effects for four item classes (40 each: expert procedural, planted wrong-procedure, location-specific 'stale-true' items whose receptacle claims hold in seen layouts only, and self-written) under four conditions on the same games and seeds: reference (Qwen3-32B, expert bank, valid_seen); reader swap to a second local backbone; store growth by the 1,892 self-pool items; and layout shift to valid_unseen. We report, per class and condition, the realized value, the fraction of items whose value sign flips, the rank correlation of the reference-trained Q with each condition's ground truth, and the episodes needed to re-validate by intervention versus the stream games needed by a re-learned Q under the new reader to reach the same rank reliability. Predictions: sign flips under reader swap are at least twice as frequent for helpful expert items as for planted wrong items; the median removal effect of expert items falls by at least half after store growth while their replace-static effect goes to zero; location-specific items are worth at least +5 net on seen and at most -5 on unseen while the stream-trained Q ranks them in the top half; and the pooled correlation of the reference Q with ground truth drops by at least 0.2 in every shifted condition. Both GPUs are busy throughout (one reader per GPU during the swap arm); about 30 GPU-pair hours.
Experiments:
- Ground-truth protocol (shared by all cells): forced-retrieval intervention on the same (game, seed). For a sampled item i of class C, take 24 same-type evaluation games x 2 seeds = 48 paired episodes with i forced into the k=3 set at rank 3 (the other two slots are the natural top-2 retrievals, or a manipulated composition). Arms per pair: WITH (i present), REMOVE (k=2 set), REPLACE-static (i replaced by the type's static procedure sentence padded to i's token count; Measurement C baseline, so REPLACE-static is item value net of the static prompt). Per-item effect = mean paired success difference; per-item SE about 0.10 at p=0.5; a 40-item class = 1,920 pairs gives a class CI of about +/-4.5 net. Cost per class per condition: 40 items x 48 pairs x 2 extra arms = 3,840 episodes = 3.2 h at 20 episodes/min on two replicas.
- E0 Cheapest first (~2 h): pilot the second backbone (candidates: Qwen3-14B or Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, whichever serves under vLLM on one A100) on 274 valid_seen games at k=0 and k=3; it is usable only if k=0 success lies in [0.30, 0.70] and the k=3 gain is >= +10 net (positive control), else the next candidate is tried. Positive control for the harm class: planted W items' REMOVE effect under the reference reader <= -10 net.
- E1 Learning pass (~3 h): per-item outcome Q (count-average and alpha=0.1) from one train-stream pass under the reference reader with the expert bank; record feedback counts. MemQ-style TD(lambda) fit on the same log as a second scorer.
- E2 Ground truth in four conditions (4 x 6.4 h): classes EP (expert procedural, positive nested-k position value), W (planted wrong-procedure, 40 items), LS (location-specific: expert items whose text names a receptacle location that holds in the seen layout; 40 selected by regex plus manual check), SW (self-written). Conditions: R = (Qwen3-32B, expert bank, valid_seen); B = (second backbone, expert bank, valid_seen); G = (Qwen3-32B, expert + self pool, valid_seen; forced item sits among the grown store's natural top-2); U = (Qwen3-32B, expert bank, valid_unseen, type-matched games). Each cell: 40 items x 24 games x 2 seeds, arms WITH / REMOVE / REPLACE-static. Sign flips are counted only for items with |value| >= 10 net in R.
- E3 Re-validation cost (~3.5 h): (i) intervention: subsample the B-condition pairs at 4, 8, 16, 24, 48 per item and compute the Spearman against the other seed half's full estimate; (ii) re-learning: run the train stream under the second backbone (3 h), fit Q_B on prefixes of 500, 1,000, 2,000 and 3,553 games, and compute the Spearman with the held-out-seed B ground truth. Report episodes to reach Spearman 0.5 for both routes, counting only episodes beyond the agent's normal operation for the stream route (zero) and total for the intervention route, and also total wall-clock episodes for both.
- E4 Lag under the learned rule: continue the reference Q online through the U-condition games (unseen stream of 274 x 2) and record, for LS items, the number of retrievals until Q crosses below the store median, versus the number of intervention pairs needed to detect the sign flip at the +/-5 net level.
- Budget: E0 2 h + E1 3 h + E2 25.6 h + E3 3.5 h + E4 0.5 h = about 35 h; during B and E3(ii) the second backbone runs on GPU 1 while the reference reader serves the G and U cells on GPU 0; nohup, pid files, resumable JSONL; pre-registration before E2.
Baselines and Ablations:
- Scorers: per-item outcome Q (reference), MemQ-style TD(lambda), usage-count control, similarity-only control; Q re-learned under the second backbone for E3.
- Ground truth: REMOVE and REPLACE-static (value net of the static procedure sentence) in every condition; the nested-k position contrast from the existing logs as the free reference for EP items.
- Composition: the G condition changes the co-retrieved set by construction; the R condition is additionally re-measured with one self-written item swapped in (second composition) so that the store-growth effect is separated from a mere set-composition change (~3.2 h, included in E2 if budget allows, else reported as pilot).
- Class ablation: LS items with the location claim edited out (token-matched) under U, to test that the sign flip is carried by the location claim and not by the rest of the item.
- Controls from prior rounds: same pool and bank-target partition in all conditions; self-pool items measured separately; token-matched placebos; memory-absent (k=0) arm per condition as the floor.

- P1 (headline) Sign-transfer asymmetry under reader swap: among items with |value| >= 10 net in R, the fraction whose REPLACE-static sign flips in B is >= 2x higher for EP than for W items (help is consumer-specific, harm transfers). Falsified if: the two flip fractions are within +/-0.10 of each other or W flips more often, with 1,000-item bootstrap CIs. Arm: E2 condition B, classes EP and W. Not entailed: a weaker reader could follow expert procedures equally well (no EP flips) or ignore wrong items (W flips), and the compliance-trap result predicts the opposite direction for weaker agents.
- P2 Store-growth substitution: the median REMOVE effect of EP items in G is <= 50% of its value in R, and their REPLACE-static effect in G is within +/-5 net of zero. Falsified if: the median REMOVE effect in G is >= 80% of R, or REPLACE-static stays >= +5 net. Arm: E2 condition G versus R on the same 40 EP items and games. Not entailed: self-written items may be worse than or non-overlapping with expert items.
- P3 Stale-true items: LS items have REPLACE-static >= +5 net in R and <= -5 net in U, and the reference-trained Q ranks the LS class median in the top half of the store. Falsified if: the U-condition LS effect is within +/-5 of zero (the reader does not act on location claims), or the LS class median Q rank is in the bottom half (the train stream already penalised them). Arm: E2 conditions R and U on the LS class; E1 Q ranks.
- P4 Validity drop: Spearman(reference Q, ground truth) pooled over the four classes falls by >= 0.20 from R to each of B, G and U. Falsified if: the drop is < 0.10 in all three, or the R correlation is itself < 0.30 (then the prediction is void and reported as a failed positive control). Arm: E2 all conditions scored by the E1 Q.
- P5 Re-validation cost: intervention on a 40-item class reaches Spearman 0.5 against held-out ground truth at <= 8 pairs per item (640 episodes per class) while the re-learned Q_B needs >= 2,000 stream games to reach 0.5 on the same items, a ratio >= 3 in total episodes. Falsified if: Q_B reaches 0.5 within 1,000 stream games, or intervention needs > 16 pairs per item. Arm: E3 (i) versus (ii) curves.
- Positive controls first: E0 second-backbone k=3 gain >= +10 net and W-class REMOVE <= -10 net under the reference reader; otherwise the study is reported as an unusable second reader or an unmanufacturable harm class, not as a null.
Measurement and Noise Control: Paired on (game, seed) across arms and, for R versus G and R versus U comparisons, on the same items; the B condition uses the same games and seeds with a different reader, so item-level differences are within-item. Class cells 40 x 48 = 1,920 pairs (+/-4.5 net). Sign flips are counted only for items whose R value clears the +/-10 net cutoff, with flip fractions bootstrapped over items. Rank correlations are disattenuated by split-seed reliability of the ground truth in each condition and reported raw as well.
